candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — expected therapeutic outcomes of spironolactone in heart failure
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the labeled heart-failure benefits of spironolactone in NYHA class III-IV reduced-ejection-fraction heart failure beyond edema management alone.

options.A: In this heart-failure population, spironolactone is indicated to increase survival, manage edema, and reduce the need for heart-failure hospitalization.
options.B: Spironolactone is used only for short-term diuresis and has no labeled benefit related to survival or heart-failure hospitalization.
options.C: Spironolactone is contraindicated in reduced-ejection-fraction heart failure because aldosterone blockade worsens ventricular function.
options.D: Spironolactone is prescribed primarily to raise serum potassium so that other heart-failure drugs can be given safely.

candidate.rationale: The current spironolactone prescribing information identifies treatment of NYHA class III-IV heart failure with reduced ejection fraction as an indication to increase survival, manage edema, and reduce the need for hospitalization for heart failure. Therefore, A is correct. B incorrectly reduces the drug to diuresis alone, C contradicts the labeled heart-failure indication, and D misstates the therapeutic purpose; spironolactone can increase potassium and requires appropriate monitoring rather than being prescribed to intentionally raise potassium.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports spironolactone use in NYHA III-IV reduced-ejection-fraction heart failure for survival, edema management, and reduction of heart-failure hospitalization need.
